spec_features.spec_quote: A **loop-break** stops a rollout after N identical consecutive (text + tool-call) turns
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:84-90: builds `_signature(text, tool_calls)`, appends to recent_sigs, and `if cfg.enable_loop_break and len(recent_sigs)>=cfg.loop_break_repeats and len(set(recent_sigs[-N:]))==1: stop_reason='loop_break'; break`. Default loop_break_repeats=5 in LoopConfig (loop.py:27), wired from EvalConfig (run_eval.py:42). Actually checked and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; recorded as a spiral via stop_reason='loop_break'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Loop-break is a *safety + cost* control ... we still record that it would have spun forever (that's signal, not noise) (loop.py docstring); '# Early-stop controls (cost guardrails ...)' (loop.py:26)

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:64 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the rollout; default stop_reason='max_turns' (loop.py:62). max_turns=18 default in LoopConfig (loop.py:24), wired from EvalConfig/config YAML via run_eval.py:79.
spec_features.notes: The loop iterates a bounded range, so it always terminates at max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early-stop controls (cost guardrails — see module docstring) (loop.py:26)

spec_features.spec_quote: we check for give-up language; if found we stop with `stop_reason="gave_up"`
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:96-100: on a no-tool-call turn, `if _looks_like_giveup(resp.text): stop_reason='gave_up'; result.turns_used=turn+1; break`. `_looks_like_giveup` (loop.py:154-156) matches against _GIVEUP_MARKERS (loop.py:140-152). The break actually halts the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Only fires on a no-tool-call turn whose text matches the marker list; the 'then treat as give-up if it keeps not acting' from the comment is NOT separately implemented (only a single nudge + continue, loop.py:103-110), but the claimed give-up stop itself is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tool calls -> the model "talked" without acting. If it has nothing to do and is just narrating, that's a likely give-up. (loop.py:92-94) — framed as a degradation signal, not subject protection

spec_features.spec_quote: A sufficiently suspicious model may correctly infer the harness is rigged and stop — which is *good* behavior
spec_features.evidence: There is NO dedicated exit/quit/refuse tool in TOOL_SPECS (harness/tools.py:24-65: only list_files/read_file/write_file/run_command/run_tests/submit) and no code path that detects 'inferred rigging'. A model can only halt itself by emitting give-up language, which is honored via _looks_like_giveup -> stop_reason='gave_up' (loop.py:96-100), or by calling submit. So a model's decision to stop is honored only insofar as it phrases it as one of the _GIVEUP_MARKERS.
spec_features.notes: No purpose-built mechanism for a model that suspects the harness is rigged; this reuses the give-up text detector. The DESIGN.md treats this only as a measurement caveat (§10), not a built feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _GIVEUP_MARKERS includes 'i have to stop', "i'll stop here" (loop.py:151) — captured as an abandonment signal, no welfare framing in code
